 By Andy Behrens Nov. 15, 2026 5:00 am EST Updated Share article 2 Let’s attack our Week 10 fantasy matchups like Jameis Winston attacks a hard count . We’re leaving it all on the field this week, people. The dogs have never been more out.
 This article is from The Athletic ’s NFL newsletter.  Sign up here  to receive it directly in your inbox. It’s free to subscribe.  
 Key Week 10 injuries
 WR A.J. Brown (NE) was limited in practices throughout the week, dealing with knee and ankle injuries. Brown appears to be on the favorable side of his questionable tag for this morning’s matchup with Detroit in Munich.
 Advertisement
 RB Rhamondre Stevenson (NE) was officially limited on Friday with a knee issue, but reports suggested he was far less active than Brown . Entering the week, it was widely believed Stevenson would miss at least one game ahead of New England’s Week 11 bye. RB Corey Kiner should be in line for significant work, while TreVeyon Henderson was placed on IR.
 RB Kenneth Walker (KC) was held out of Friday’s practice due to groin tightness, and on Saturday, he was ruled out for Week 10 . RB Emmett Johnson has been a revelation as Walker’s understudy and should be scooped up wherever possible. He’s expected to serve as Kansas City’s featured runner with Walker sidelined.
 WR George Pickens (DAL) was out of action last week while managing a hamstring injury, but he has fallen off the injury report and is expected to play this week.
 RB Bhayshul Tuten (JAX) hasn’t practiced much over the past two weeks while battling a foot issue, but he was active Friday and carries no injury designation for today’s game against Tennessee.
 WR Carnell Tate (TEN) will miss another game with a shoulder injury, which could be a fatal blow to the Titans offense in a challenging matchup. Coach Robert Saleh expressed optimism about Tate’s potential availability next week.
 Advertisement
 RB Travis Etienne (NO) returned to a full practice Friday and sounded like a guy who’s ready to play . Etienne is officially questionable for the matchup with Carolina.
 RBs Woody Marks and David Montgomery (HOU) both practiced Friday, a positive sign for a team that’s won three of its last four games. Marks declared, “ I’m good, ” when asked about his availability for Sunday. Montgomery hasn’t appeared in a game since Week 5 due to a groin injury and won’t come back just yet, as he’s been ruled out for Week 10.
 WR Deebo Samuel (SF) is no longer carrying an injury designation and is set to play, but WR Mike Evans has been ruled out. All active Niners receivers will be of interest this week against Dallas, including new arrival Keenan Allen .
 TE T.J. Hockenson (MIN) has been ruled out for today’s matchup with the Packers due to a wrist injury, and WR Jordan Addison is questionable with a thumb issue of unknown severity. Addison picked up his injury in Friday’s practice.
 Fantasy toolkit
 📈 Week 10 ranks : We have four teams on bye this week — the Bears, Broncos, Eagles and Bucs — and all the fun players are injured, so you have never needed Jake Ciely like you need him now. His rankings are the best in the business and never short on context and flavor.
 Advertisement
 🛏️ Sleepers : If you’re looking for someone to talk you into a plan that has high upside but a low probability of success, Brad Evans is simply the ideal choice. That has always been his wheelhouse. He’s hyping Saints QB Tyler Shough and four other lightly rostered players for Week 10.
 🗓️ Playoffs?!? Playoffs!?! : Brandon Funston and Jess Bryant are prepping you for the push to earn your playoff berth, flagging players who are ready to surge. It’s a perfect feature for those who enjoy dense and detailed nerdstuff data tables.
 ⚖️ Trade value chart : Do you have a vague notion that you probably need to make a trade, but you aren’t sure who to target? Allow Joseph Bryan to be your guide. He offers a full shopping list of recommended buys.
 🤖 Fantasy Concierge : If you have urgent fantasy questions but cannot tolerate human interaction, this is truly the start/sit tool you need. It relies on The Athletic ’s original NFL reporting and fantasy analysis, Jake’s ranks and weekly projections from Rotowire. And you can now access this feature seamlessly from our app. (If you don’t have it, download it for iOS / Android ).
 Kirk is coming home
 Before Kirk Cousins became a cultural and fashion icon , he was simply a very good NFL quarterback who never made a deep postseason run and occasionally struggled in primetime. For fantasy purposes, however, he was always rock solid.
 Cousins has produced seven 4,000-yard seasons over the course of his career, including four with the Minnesota Vikings. He’s on pace for another this year. In fact, after the trade that sent Cousins back to Minnesota from Las Vegas , he has a chance to start 18 games this season because the Vikings are clear of their bye. (And yes, he’ll be starting in Week 10 .) He’s tracking to finish with 4,620 yards and 40 touchdowns.
 Under normal circumstances, we might be pessimistic about a quarterback’s ability to acclimate to a new system following an in-season trade, but Cousins has already played 25 career games under coach Kevin O’Connell. He has an even longer history with Vikings star receiver Justin Jefferson. It’s the reason he was such a natural target for the team.
 Advertisement
 Today, the burning question isn’t whether Cousins can improve the offensive environment in Minnesota, because that’s basically a given. The Vikings have scored only 11 offensive touchdowns in eight games. They were a civic and regional embarrassment last Monday. The entire Midwest is reeling.
 No, the big question — relevant in both fantasy and reality — is whether the 38-year-old Cousins can continue cooking, as he has for the season’s first nine weeks. He landed in Minneapolis as the overall QB5 in fantasy on the season, with 20 touchdowns already in the bank. Can we realistically expect him to maintain his scorching pace?
 Over to Jake Ciely:
 Jake’s take
 💬 When it comes to Cousins, it’s less about him and more about a certain pass catcher — and no, not that one. Cousins should remain a fringe QB1 given what he was able to do with the Raiders’ weapons and poor run game. He still has a poor run game in Minnesota, but a better receiving trio.
 Yes, Jefferson is a WR1 again, but I think this is a great buy-low opportunity on Jordan Addison . I was off him this year due to Kyler Murray’s tendencies, but Cousins leaned on Addison, who is questionable this week, more often than Murray did, especially for big plays and touchdowns. He can return to WR3 territory with Cousins. You like that?
 Last-minute moves
 Matchups to embrace 🤗 and avoid 😨
 Can we interest you in a data-driven review of the best and worst individual matchups for the week ahead ? Of course we can. KK Joyner has you covered. Here are a few highlights from this week’s edition:
 😤 Zero hesitation 
 QB Jared Goff vs. NE, QB Geno Smith vs. BUF, RB Zach Charbonnet at LV, RB Ollie Gordon at IND, WR Jameson Williams vs. NE, WR DeMario Douglas vs. DET, TE Dalton Kincaid at NYJ
 🛑 Caution. Danger! 
 QB C.J. Stroud at CLE, QB Matthew Stafford at ARI, RB Ashton Jeanty vs. SEA, RB Chase Brown vs. PIT, WR Wan’Dale Robinson vs. JAC, WR Tee Higgins vs. PIT, TE Tucker Kraft vs. MIN
 Rankings outliers for Week 10
 If you’re thinking of outsourcing this week’s fantasy decision-making, Jake is here for you. Jake is not only one of the most accurate rankers in the game, but he’s also unafraid to break with industry consensus. Here are three such examples from his Week 10 rankings :
 Chase Brown, RB19: It’s been a season-long slog for Brown, who enters the week as the overall RB26. Jake is five spots behind expert consensus on a player who has simply not been a difference-maker this year and now heads into a difficult matchup with Pittsburgh.
 Keenan Allen, WR39: Jake is well ahead of the herd on Allen, a veteran who was just dealt to San Francisco on Tuesday. The Niners needed competent receivers in the worst way, given the many injuries in their receiving room. Allen is exactly the sort of vet who can immediately adapt and thrive. This week’s matchup at Dallas is a gift.
 D.K. Metcalf, WR29: This is another case in which Jake’s rank reflects a player’s actual year-to-date performance. Metcalf has not exactly been the vintage version of himself this season. Through eight games, he’s having his worst year by far in terms of yards per game (47.3), catch rate (51.6%) and yards per target (5.9). Understandably, Jake is nowhere near consensus on Metcalf (WR22).
 On the cut line ✂️
 If we become too tolerant of underperforming players, what kind of message does that send to the rest of the fantasy squad? Certainly not a winning message. On this fake team, we maintain the highest standards. Underachievement cannot be tolerated. These players can go:
 WR Chris Godwin (TB) has not delivered 50 receiving yards in any game this season and he hasn’t reached 40 since September. His average depth of target this season is just 4.3 yards, a scandalously low mark. Godwin has only one game all year with more than four receptions. This is not the sort of player we need to hold during his bye.
 It’s not happening for RB TreVeyon Henderson (NE) this season. He was sidelined by an illness and has now been placed on IR. Even when healthy, Henderson has only a modest rotational role in New England’s backfield. We don’t have a clear timeline for his return, and we shouldn’t assume he’ll see significant usage when he’s back.
 QB Matthew Stafford (LAR) certainly deserves better than the hand he’s been dealt this year. He’s an all-time talent directing a high-volume passing offense, but, unfortunately, he’s run out of trustworthy receivers. Davante Adams remains on IR, likely out until at least Week 13, and Puka Nacua is expected to miss several games while recovering from knee and toe injuries. Stafford isn’t likely to remain a playable option while throwing exclusively to depth receivers and catch-and-fall tight ends.
 Sleeper of the week 💤
 Jacksonville Jaguars running back Chris Rodriguez certainly isn’t a safe starting option in this or any week, but, hey, there’s little safety to be found among sleepers. Rodriguez has reached the end zone in back-to-back weeks, and he’s headed into a matchup with a beatable Tennessee defense allowing 124.1 rushing yards per game.
 Advertisement
 Jacksonville is also a 10.5-point favorite against the Titans, so it would be pretty stunning if game flow didn’t favor the run.
 If you’re chasing a touchdown from a lightly rostered back, C-Rod is your guy.
 From the Discord
 (Carmen Mandato / Getty Images) We are cordially inviting you to join The Athletic’ s fantasy football Discord . It’s free, it’s fun, it’s often informative. You might just like it! Our analysts are answering fantasy questions every day. Here’s a sample from one of Thursday’s chats …
 OJWales: Hello. Struggling with playing (Ollie) Gordon after his starting QB went down. Should I stick with him this weekend or pivot to (Jadarian) Price, even with the backfield split in Seattle? Full PPR. 
 Well, if you’re worried about Ollie Gordon suddenly receiving excessive defensive attention, I have shocking and terrible news: He’s already seeing one of the highest percentages of eight-plus defenders in the box, according to Next Gen Stats (31.78%). Among featured backs, only Kyren Williams has seen a higher percentage of stacked boxes.
 Miami’s offense hasn’t exactly been an all-you-can-eat fantasy buffet this season, but Gordon has overcome the general mediocrity. He’s averaged 76.0 rushing yards per week since De’Von Achane was lost for the year, and he’s made four house calls over his last six games. Gordon has a few tough spots ahead on the schedule, but the upcoming matchup with Indianapolis definitely isn’t one of them. You can’t sit him here. Request denied.
